notice: This is technical evidence from an automated scan, offered as supporting material for an ISO/IEC 27001:2022 assessment. It does not decide whether any control is implemented or effective, it is not an audit, and it is not a certificate. Each statement cites the scan output it comes from; each control lists what that evidence cannot show.

controls.title: Inventory of information and other associated assets

evidence.statement: Software bill of materials lists 12 component(s) in CycloneDX 1.5 format.
AI component inventory lists 0 component(s) and 1 model reference(s), 1 of them not pinned to a version.

limits: Only software components and AI models/agents declared in this repository are listed; information assets, data stores, hardware and services are not.
An inventory shows what exists, not who owns it, how it is classified, or that it is kept current.

controls.title: Authentication information

evidence.statement: Secret scanning of the working tree ran (scope: secrets). No open findings.

limits: A clean secret scan shows no recognizable credential was found in the scanned files; it does not show credentials are generated, stored, rotated or revoked well.
Secrets already committed to git history are only covered when a history scan was run, which findings.json does not record.
Password rules, multi-factor authentication and credential allocation are processes outside the repository.

controls.title: Information security in supplier relationships

evidence.statement: Software bill of materials lists 12 component(s) in CycloneDX 1.5 format.

limits: The bill of materials names third-party software suppliers; it shows nothing about the agreements, assessments or monitoring that govern the relationship.

controls.title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain

evidence.statement: Software bill of materials lists 12 component(s) in CycloneDX 1.5 format.
Supply-chain checks (slopsquatting, provenance, licenses, containers) ran (scope: supply-chain). No open findings.

limits: Checks cover dependencies declared in lockfiles and manifests; build tooling, hosted services and vendored binaries outside them are not covered.
Provenance and typosquat checks flag risk signals; they do not verify a supplier's own security practices.
Requirements placed on suppliers and the process for acting on supply-chain change are not visible to a scan.

controls.title: Information security for use of cloud services

evidence.statement: Infrastructure-as-code configuration checks ran (scope: iac). No open findings.

gaps: Infrastructure-as-code configuration checks found nothing, but the scan outputs do not show that any files of this kind were present. No findings may mean there was nothing to check.
limits: Only cloud configuration declared in files in this repository is checked; the deployed state of a cloud account is not observed.
Choice of provider, the shared-responsibility split, contractual terms and exit arrangements are outside what a scan can see.

controls.title: Privacy and protection of personal identifiable information (PII)

evidence.statement: Sensitive-data handling checks ran (scope: data). No open findings.

gaps: Sensitive-data handling checks found nothing, but the scan outputs do not show that any files of this kind were present. No findings may mean there was nothing to check.
limits: Checks look for patterns that suggest personal data is handled unsafely in code; they cannot decide what is personal data in your context.
Lawful basis, records of processing, retention, data-subject rights and impact assessments are not visible to a scan.

controls.title: Access to source code

evidence.statement: Secret scanning (credentials that would expose code or systems) ran (scope: secrets). No open findings.

limits: Nox does not see who can read or write the repository, branch protection, review requirements or access reviews; those are repository-host settings.
The only technical evidence is indirect: whether credentials are committed to the working tree.

controls.title: Management of technical vulnerabilities

evidence.statement: Dependency vulnerability checks against OSV.dev ran (scope: deps). 2 open finding(s): 1 high, 1 medium. 2 of them name a version that fixes them. Also 1 finding(s) baselined, suppressed or VEX-cleared.
Software bill of materials lists 12 component(s) in CycloneDX 1.5 format.

gaps: Dependency vulnerability checks against OSV.dev: 1 finding(s) are waived, baselined or VEX-cleared. Each is a decision to accept or defer a risk; the scan does not show who made it or why, and a reviewer will ask.
limits: Only vulnerabilities in declared dependencies are covered; operating systems, base images not described in the repository, and running infrastructure are not.
A finding is a published advisory against a package version. Whether the vulnerable code is reachable in your application is a separate question the finding states per case.
Evidence of a vulnerability management process (who is told, how quickly it is fixed, which risks are accepted and by whom) is not in a scan.

controls.title: Configuration management

evidence.statement: Infrastructure and file-permission configuration checks ran (scope: iac). No open findings.

gaps: Infrastructure and file-permission configuration checks found nothing, but the scan outputs do not show that any files of this kind were present. No findings may mean there was nothing to check.
limits: Checks cover configuration written in this repository against known-risky settings; they are not a baseline you approved.
Whether configuration in production matches the repository, and how changes to it are authorized, is not observed.

controls.title: Data leakage prevention

evidence.statement: Sensitive-data and secret-exposure checks ran (scope: data). No open findings.

limits: Static checks find code that may expose data; they are not a data-leakage-prevention control operating on networks, endpoints or mail.
Data classification and the rules for handling each class are organizational.

controls.title: Use of cryptography

evidence.statement: Weak or misused cryptography checks ran (scope: code). 1 open finding(s): 1 medium.

limits: Checks find weak algorithms, protocols and settings in code and configuration; they do not assess key generation, storage, rotation or retirement.
A policy on cryptography and the records of how keys are managed are organizational.

controls.title: Secure development life cycle

evidence.statement: Record of the security scan itself: a scan by nox 1.2.3 on 2026-10-24T17:18:36Z covered all scopes with 4 active finding(s) in total. It shows a security scan was run, not that one runs on every change.

limits: One scan shows that a security check ran once. It does not show the check runs on every change, that findings block release, or that the rules of the life cycle are defined.

controls.title: Application security requirements
limits: Requirements are written down by people before code exists. Nothing a scan produces states, or tests conformance to, your requirements.

controls.title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles

evidence.statement: AI component inventory (models, agents, tools) lists 0 component(s) and 1 model reference(s), 1 of them not pinned to a version.
AI, agent and MCP architecture checks ran (scope: ai). No open findings.

limits: Checks examine a few architectural risks in AI-enabled applications (tool exposure, trust boundaries); they are not a review of the architecture.
Documented principles, threat models and design reviews are organizational.

controls.title: Secure coding

evidence.statement: Static analysis of application code ran (scope: code). 1 open finding(s): 1 high.

limits: Static analysis finds a subset of defect classes in the languages it supports; absence of findings is not absence of defects.
Coding standards, developer training and code review practice are organizational.

controls.title: Security testing in development and acceptance

evidence.statement: Record of the security scan itself: a scan by nox 1.2.3 on 2026-10-24T17:18:36Z covered all scopes with 4 active finding(s) in total. It shows a security scan was run, not that one runs on every change.

gaps: No dynamic verification was performed in this scan: findings are static observations, none was confirmed exploitable or shown to be prevented. Run `nox attack` against a running target for runtime evidence.
limits: Static scanning is one kind of security testing. Penetration tests, acceptance tests and test plans are not produced by it.

organizational_evidence_required.title: ISMS scope
organizational_evidence_required.needed: A statement of what the information security management system covers, and where this repository and the product built from it sit inside that boundary.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Information security policy
organizational_evidence_required.needed: An approved policy and the topic-specific policies beneath it, communicated to the people they apply to.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Roles and responsibilities
organizational_evidence_required.needed: Named owners for information security, including who owns security of this application.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Risk assessment, treatment and Statement of Applicability
organizational_evidence_required.needed: A documented risk method, a risk register that includes this application, treatment decisions with owners (including any accepted risk), and the Statement of Applicability that records which Annex A controls apply and why.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Security objectives
organizational_evidence_required.needed: Measurable objectives and the records of how they are monitored.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Competence, awareness and training
organizational_evidence_required.needed: Records that developers and operators have the skills the role needs, including secure-coding training.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Documented information control
organizational_evidence_required.needed: How documents and records are created, approved, versioned and retained, so that this assessment material is itself a controlled record.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Internal audit and management review
organizational_evidence_required.needed: An audit programme with reports, and minutes of management review of the system's performance.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Nonconformity and continual improvement
organizational_evidence_required.needed: A record of nonconformities, corrective actions and their closure.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Asset ownership
organizational_evidence_required.needed: An inventory covering information, services and data stores beyond software components, each with an owner.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Data classification and handling
organizational_evidence_required.needed: A classification scheme, labelling and handling rules, and evidence they are applied to this application's data.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Privacy records
organizational_evidence_required.needed: Records of processing, lawful basis, retention rules and data-protection impact assessments for personal data this application handles.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Access control and access reviews
organizational_evidence_required.needed: An access control policy, evidence of periodic access reviews, joiner/mover/leaver records, and the repository-host settings that restrict who can read and change source code.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Supplier agreements and reviews
organizational_evidence_required.needed: Supplier security requirements in contracts, assessments of the suppliers the software bill of materials implies, and how supplier service changes are monitored.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Cloud service governance
organizational_evidence_required.needed: A cloud-use policy, the shared-responsibility split agreed with each provider, and exit arrangements.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Incident management
organizational_evidence_required.needed: A documented incident process, roles, and records of incidents and exercises, including how a vulnerability disclosed in a dependency is handled.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Continuity, backup and redundancy
organizational_evidence_required.needed: Continuity plans and backup/restore test records for the systems this application runs on.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Logging and monitoring
organizational_evidence_required.needed: Evidence that production logs are collected, protected and reviewed, and that anomalies raise alerts someone acts on.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Cryptography and key management
organizational_evidence_required.needed: A cryptography policy and records of how keys and secrets are generated, stored, rotated and revoked.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Vulnerability management process
organizational_evidence_required.needed: Time-to-remediate targets, triage records, and the approval trail for any vulnerability left unfixed.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Change and configuration management
organizational_evidence_required.needed: A change process with approvals, and configuration baselines that production is compared against.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Secure development procedure
organizational_evidence_required.needed: A defined development life cycle with security gates, code review rules, and evidence they run on every change (for example CI configuration and review records).

organizational_evidence_required.title: Application security requirements
organizational_evidence_required.needed: Documented security requirements for this application and traceability from them to tests.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Architecture principles and threat modelling
organizational_evidence_required.needed: Documented secure-engineering principles and threat models or design reviews for this application.

organizational_evidence_required.title: Security testing plan and results
organizational_evidence_required.needed: A testing plan, penetration test reports and acceptance-test records, with findings tracked to closure.
